title: Ref safety follow-up: reject % outright, and decide the write-side question
description:
Follow-up required by TASK-185's AC5 and its LOW-1, both recorded at close. Two related items on the same control.

**Item 1 — the percent-encoding defense is narrower than the docs that ship with it (LOW-1).**

`UNSAFE_REF_RE` matches only the literal token `%2e%2e`. The TASK-185 reviewer executed the committed guard against adjacent forms and found these pass through:

```
"%252e%252e/x"             (double-encoded)
"..%2fx"  "..%5cx"         (literal .. with an encoded separator)
"..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswd"
"x%2f..%2fetc"
"....//etc/passwd"         (naive ../-stripper bait)
"a%00/etc/passwd"
```

None is exploitable today: every one needs a consumer that percent-decodes or naively strips `../` BEFORE resolving, and no such consumer exists — agents open a ref as a literal repo-relative path. That is why it closed as LOW rather than blocking.

The part that does matter is the overclaim. `skills/orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md:997` and the `kb_graph_query` tool description at `src/mcp-server.js:550` both tell agents the guard covers refs "disguised via ... percent-encoding" with no qualification. False confidence in a control is the exact failure class this repo keeps paying for.

**Recommended fix (from the reviewer, and it is a good one): reject any ref containing `%` outright.** Evidence it is safe: the reviewer ran all 225 refs currently in `knowledge/graph/graph.json` through the guard and **zero contain a `%`**. So the false-negative cost is provably zero today, and it replaces a token blacklist — which loses arms races by construction — with a whitelist-shaped rule. If that is adopted, the docs become true rather than needing softening.

**Item 2 — the write side (TASK-185 AC5's deferred question).**

`GRAPH_SCHEMA` in `src/knowledge-graph.js` has `ref: {type: 'string', minLength: 1}` and validates no shape, so an unsafe ref can still be WRITTEN into `knowledge/graph/graph.json`. It simply will not be surfaced by `kb_graph_query`.

The TASK-185 reviewer assessed this as **correctly scoped out and NOT a weakness**, with reasoning worth preserving: `safeRef` sits at the point of consumption — the only place a ref becomes an instruction to open a file — so the control is complete regardless of what is stored. Schema hardening would be defense-in-depth, would be a genuine trust-boundary change, and **would break existing graphs at load time**.

So this ticket must not assume the write side needs hardening. Decide it deliberately: either add write-side validation with a migration path for the existing 225-node graph, or record an explicit decision that consumption-point validation is the right and sufficient boundary. Both are legitimate outcomes; an undecided residual is not.
acceptance_criteria: A failing spec first demonstrates the current residuals: '..%2fx', '..%5cx', '%252e%252e/x' and '....//etc/passwd' currently pass through safeRef unchanged. Capture the red-run output verbatim as the tests-first evidence.

Item 1 is resolved by a rule that does not lose an arms race. If the recommended '%'-rejection is adopted, first re-verify against the CURRENT knowledge/graph/graph.json that zero live refs contain '%' (the 225-ref figure is from 2026-08-02 and the graph grows every close) — do not rely on the recorded number.

The docs stop overclaiming: skills/orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md and the kb_graph_query tool description describe exactly what the guard does and does not cover. Both SKILL.md parity copies byte-identical.

Item 2 is DECIDED and the decision recorded in the closing comment: either write-side validation lands with a proven migration path for the existing graph, or an explicit reasoned decision that consumption-point validation is the sufficient boundary. An undecided residual is not an acceptable close.

If write-side validation IS adopted, prove it does not break the existing graph at load time — run the real knowledge/graph/graph.json through the new schema and show the result. This is the specific risk the TASK-185 reviewer flagged.
No regression in false-negative behaviour: every ref in the live graph must still pass through unchanged after the fix. Show the count.
npm run test:all is green; dist/mcp-server.cjs rebuilt via npm run build:plugin and committed, with tests/e2e/dist-parity.spec.js passing.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
APPROVED and closed on a green FULL-depth review. **0 HIGH / 0 MEDIUM / 2 LOW.**

**Review depth: FULL.** Rubric inputs: ~195 changed lines across 6 files; the change is to a **security guard** (`UNSAFE_REF_RE`, the path-traversal defense at the only seam where a stored `ref` becomes an instruction to open a file), plus a shipped `dist/mcp-server.cjs` rebuild; tier `tdd`.

## AC4 — the write-side decision, recorded here as the AC requires

**Write-side validation NOT adopted. Consumption-point validation is sufficient.**

`safeRef` sits at the READ boundary — the only place a stored `ref` becomes an instruction to open a file — so the control is complete regardless of what shape is stored. Write-side hardening would be defense-in-depth carrying real migration risk across 233 existing graph nodes, for no consumer-facing benefit, since no write path decodes or resolves a ref either. **AC5 is therefore not applicable** — no schema change was made, so there is no load-time migration to prove.

**The premise was verified, not assumed.** The reviewer enumerated every consumer of `ref` across `src/`, `bin/`, and `scripts/`:

1. `src/mcp-server.js:661/666` — all three node-returning branches of `kb_graph_query` route through `sortNodesById` → `safeRef`. The only surface that hands a ref to an agent instructed to open it.
2. `src/task-board.js:1097/1169` — renders `node.ref` as inert text (`textContent`/`escHtml`). Display only; no XSS vector.
3. `src/graph-sync.js:40` — forwards `ref` as `source_ref` metadata on the write direction; no file open.
4. `src/graph-freshness.js` — reads node ids only.
5. `src/knowledge-graph.js:178` — returns raw refs, but its exported consumers are reached only through the guarded mcp-server paths.
6. `bin/` — zero matches.

**No code path anywhere does `join(repoRoot, ref)` + read.** The decision is sound, not hollow.

## Item 1 — the guard, and the over-tightening adjudication

`UNSAFE_REF_RE` went from `/^[/\\~]|^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]*:|(?:^|[/\\])\.\.(?:[/\\]|$)|%2e%2e/i` to `/^[/\\~]|^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]*:|\.\.|%/i` — `..` now matched **unanchored**, and **any `%`** rejected outright.

Verified independently by both the Orchestrator and the reviewer against the live graph:

- **233 refs; 0 blocked by the old regex, 0 blocked by the new** — zero false-negative regression (AC6).
- **Coverage regression: 0** — the new regex blocks everything the old one blocked.
- **All seven AC1 residuals** (`%252e%252e/x`, `..%2fx`, `..%5cx`, `..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswd`, `x%2f..%2fetc`, `....//etc/passwd`, `a%00/etc/passwd`) passed through the old guard and are blocked by the new one.
- Fresh `%`-in-live-refs count: **0 of 233** (up from the ticket's stale 225 figure).

**Over-tightening: ACCEPTED, deliberately.** The Orchestrator found two plausible casualties the ticket never considered — `notes/v1.2..v1.3-diff.md` (`..` is git's own range syntax) and `reports/100%-coverage.md`. Both are now refused. The reviewer adjudicated: zero live refs affected, and both fail closed into the documented `ref: null` → fall-back-to-`id`/`label` contract — a refused convenience, never a hole or an error. The narrower alternative (separator-flanked `..`) is **precisely what admitted `..%2fx`** in the first place. Losing a filename convention is the right trade against losing the arms race.

## Item 3 — docs, verified clause by clause

Every clause checked against source rather than read for plausibility — the discipline this session had to learn three times over: `^[/\\~]` = absolute + `~` + UNC; `^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]*:` = URL scheme including single-letter Windows drive; `\.\.` = unanchored substring; `%` = anywhere; and the whitespace/CR-LF clause correctly attributed to the **separate** code path at `src/mcp-server.js:148`, not to the regex. The "raw string check / no decoding / complete only because no consumer decodes or `../`-strips first" qualifier is true per the consumer audit above.

**AC6's live-graph spec is non-vacuous by construction** — it asserts `refs.length > 0` before looping, directly closing the instance-3 empty-checked-set failure mode, and a neutered `safeRef` fails on the first ref.

## Gate

`test:since -- 3d9c0df~1` 17 files / 189 tests ⬛ `npm test` 83 files / 1113 passed ⬛ `safe-ref.spec.js` 19/19 ⬛ kb-graph-query + mcp-server + dist-parity 30 tests ⬛ `npm run test:all` **181 files / 2088 passed** ⬛ `check:calibration` clean ⬛ parity byte-identical `9eefccc7…` ⬛ dist genuine rebuild containing the exact new regex, only that bundle changed.

## MEDIUM discharged — the R3 checklist exists

The reviewer reviews cold and correctly declined to raise a finding on absent evidence. Confirming from the hand-off: all five items were stated. (1) Unspecced path — grepped all `safeRef` callers, found exactly one (`sortNodesById`), already covered; reviewed the neighboring `readTask`/`KEY_RE` guard for interaction, none. (2) Red-green planted — AC1's red captured verbatim, and AC6's live-graph lock additionally planted by forcing `safeRef` to return `null` (3 of 19 red), then restored to a zero-diff tree. (3) dist rebuilt, only `mcp-server.cjs` changed. (4) Parity hash-confirmed. (5) Calibration n/a.

## LOW carried forward

1. `src/mcp-server.js:127-128` — the comment *"Case-insensitive (`i`) so an uppercase scheme is still caught"* is a **false rationale**: `[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]*` already matches uppercase without the flag, and after this change the regex contains no case-sensitive atoms at all, so `i` is functionally inert (it previously earned its keep on `%2e%2e`). Behaviour is identical either way, hence LOW — but a wrong explanation inside a security-guard comment is exactly the intent-vs-source drift class this ticket exists to eliminate. Drop the flag or mark it inert on the next touch.
2. Informational — the over-tightening residual (legitimate filenames containing `..` or `%` become un-referenceable via `ref`) is accepted per the adjudication above and derivable from the documented rule. Optionally name it explicitly in the SKILL on a future doc touch.
